clue.text: Coins not likely to depreciate suddenly in value?

definitions.text: Coins not likely to depreciate suddenly in value?

parts.words: Coins not likely to depreciate suddenly in value?
parts.note: money of a strong, stable nation, whose worth holds firm on the exchanges, read as metal that will not soften

explanation.surface: A collector wonders which coins will keep their worth.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong, stable money is one whose exchange value is not expected to fall sharply.

clue.text: Where bowlers go, perhaps, after being taken off

definitions.text: Where bowlers go, perhaps, after being taken off

parts.words: Where bowlers go, perhaps, after being taken off
parts.note: bowlers here are bowler hats, removed indoors and hung on pegs, not cricketers taken off by the captain

explanation.surface: Cricket bowlers retire to somewhere after the captain replaces them.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket reading (a bowler 'taken off' is replaced in the attack) misleads; a bowler is also a hard round felt hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand of pegs in a hallway is where removed hats, such as bowlers, are hung.

clue.text: A tangle of reeds or an ornamental screen

indicators.note: a tangle jumbles things together, so the letters that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: Reeds knotted together are offered as an alternative to a decorative screen.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the decorated panel or screen standing behind a church altar.

clue.text: Afraid of getting shot?

parts.note: the shot is a photograph, not a bullet: someone who dislikes being photographed

explanation.surface: Someone fears being fired on.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes a person who dislikes being photographed, a photo being a 'shot'.

clue.text: A sovereign state

parts.note: a country ruled by a monarch, the domain of a sovereign

explanation.surface: A self-governing nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A kingdom is a land under a sovereign's rule.

clue.text: Devoured as the food was by those who took flight?

definitions.text: as the food was by those who took flight?
definitions.meaning: the in-flight meal was consumed while the passengers were aloft, 'up' in the air

explanation.surface: Airline passengers wolf down their meals.
explanation.definitionFit: Devoured means consumed entirely; food eaten by air travellers was also consumed high in the sky.

clue.text: Dismayed actor taking first class return in Yugoslavia

indicators.note: dismayed suggests being thrown into disorder, so the letters of the word actor are rearranged
a return journey goes back, so the letters for first class are read backwards

parts.note: A1, written A-one, here AI, means first class

explanation.surface: An upset actor travels back first class within Yugoslavia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dismayed' rearranges ACTOR to CROAT; 'return' turns AI (A1, first class) into IA. The definition 'in Yugoslavia' refers to the republic that was part of Yugoslavia until 1991.
explanation.definitionFit: The Balkan republic was one of the constituent states of the former Yugoslavia.

clue.text: Words of cheer

parts.note: a cheer here is a shout of acclamation, the traditional three-part call before a crowd shouts in celebration

explanation.surface: Encouraging remarks.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the traditional shout raised in celebration, a literal cheer.

clue.text: call round and start in the meantime

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'call round and start in the meantime', begins lowercase and looks cut short; no parse gives INTERIM from these words alone and a search found no fuller text.
annotationWithheld.clue: call round and start in the meantime

clue.text: City whose inhabitants Paul and Barnabas invited to a chin-wag?

definitions.text: City whose inhabitants Paul and Barnabas invited to a chin-wag?

parts.words: City whose inhabitants Paul and Barnabas invited to a chin-wag?
parts.note: in Acts, Paul and Barnabas preached in this Syrian city; the chin-wag reads the city's name as a chat with a relative

explanation.surface: The apostles Paul and Barnabas call a city's people in for a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: In Acts 13, Paul and Barnabas preach in the synagogue of this city in Pisidia; the 'chin-wag' plays on its name sounding like a friendly natter.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the ancient city where Paul and Barnabas preached, according to the Book of Acts.

clue.text: The capital way in which top men operate in the private sector

definitions.text: The capital way in which top men operate in the private sector

parts.words: The capital way in which top men operate in the private sector
parts.note: a road in London, the capital, where eminent surgeons perform operations for private patients

explanation.surface: Business leaders run private firms in the metropolis's manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Operate' means perform surgery, not run a business, and 'way' is a road. HARLEY STREET is the London street famous for private medical consultants.
explanation.definitionFit: This London street is known for private doctors and surgeons, top medics who perform operations there.

clue.text: Dora strangely inhibited by her niggardly personality

indicators.note: something inhibited is held in, so the reworked name sits inside the word her

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: strangely says the name Dora is put into an odd new order

explanation.surface: Dora is oddly held back by her stingy character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inhibited by' reads as restraint in the surface, but it is the container signal: the jumbled name sits inside the possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser who stockpiles and won't spend has a stingy, mean nature.

clue.text: NCB employee describing short thoroughfare of which York is particularly proud

definitions.text: of which York is particularly proud

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw round it, so the worker's title goes around the road abbreviation

parts.note: the NCB was the National Coal Board, which employed coal miners
St is the short form of Street

explanation.surface: A coal worker talks about a little street that York is proud of.
explanation.walkthrough: The NCB was Britain's nationalised coal industry (National Coal Board). 'describing' means drawing round, so the worker encloses the street.
explanation.definitionFit: York's great cathedral church, its famous Gothic landmark, is a source of civic pride.

clue.text: Weapons once used for attacking Lakeland summits?

definitions.meaning: long spears formerly carried by foot soldiers
in the English Lake District, peaked hills are called by this name, as in Scafell

explanation.surface: Old weapons were used to storm the mountain tops of the Lake District.
explanation.walkthrough: Lakeland is the Lake District in north-west England, where peaks are often named this way (Scafell Pike).
explanation.definitionFit: These are long-shafted infantry spears, and also a Cumbrian word for pointed hilltops.

clue.text: A spot of security

parts.note: spot means a location, not a small amount: somewhere protected from harm or theft

explanation.surface: A little bit of protection.
explanation.definitionFit: A secure location where something is protected is literally a spot offering safety.

clue.text: Wild deer outwardly doomed though in league with one another?

indicators.note: the word for doomed stays on the outside, enclosing the jumbled animal

parts.note: doomed means fated

indicators.note: wild suggests disorder, so the word deer is jumbled

explanation.surface: Wild deer, though doomed, stick together in a pack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' reorders the animal to EDER, and 'outwardly' keeps the word for doomed on the outside of it.
explanation.definitionFit: States joined in a federation are allied under one union, banded together.

clue.text: A den you'll find inordinately pure

indicators.note: inordinately means beyond proper order, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: You'll discover a den that is excessively pristine.
explanation.definitionFit: Unmixed with any other metal, so undiluted and wholly unadulterated.

clue.text: Feckless fellow after an outlet for trade in Belgium

indicators.note: after places the fellow later in the word, following the article

parts.note: taken as written
a twerp is a silly, ineffectual person

explanation.surface: A useless man is chasing a market in Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: This Flemish city is one of Europe's great seaports, a major outlet for commerce.

clue.text: A salmon-spear rendered sterile

indicators.note: rendered means made into something else, so the letters of sterile are reshaped

explanation.surface: A fishing spear has been made germ-free.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a pronged fishing spear used, chiefly in Scotland, for taking salmon.

clue.text: Sends off the stakes?

definitions.meaning: wooden poles driven into the ground

explanation.surface: Someone dispatches the money bets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stakes' suggests wagers, but here it means poles in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispatch by mail, and also upright wooden poles such as fence supports.

clue.text: Rustic who grows vegetables beneath which there's an insect

indicators.note: in a down entry, the second piece sits beneath the first

parts.note: peas are green vegetables
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A country dweller tends a vegetable patch where insects crawl underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: A countryman, especially a small farmer or farm labourer.

clue.text: A top delivery-man who subtly takes over?

definitions.meaning: a child's toy that twirls on its point
a cricketer whose deliveries turn; in cricket, a bowler 'takes' an over of six balls

explanation.surface: A senior courier quietly assumes control.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an 'over' is a set of six balls from one bowler; 'delivery' is a ball bowled. The surface's takeover is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: A twirling toy, and a cricket bowler who imparts turn on the ball.

clue.text: Response to a call for fresh judgment

definitions.text: Response to a call for fresh judgment

parts.words: Response to a call for fresh judgment
parts.note: an appeal in court asks for the case to be decided again, and a court may grant a new hearing

explanation.surface: A reply to someone demanding a new verdict.
explanation.definitionFit: A case heard again before a court, often ordered after a successful appeal.

clue.text: Reindeer owners swallowing soft drinks?

indicators.note: swallowing takes something in, so the word for drinks encloses the musical letter

parts.note: laps means drinks, as a cat does
p (piano) is the musical abbreviation for soft

explanation.surface: Herdsmen of reindeer gulp down fizzy drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soft drinks' looks like one phrase (sodas), but 'soft' gives P and 'drinks' gives LAPS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sami people of northern Scandinavia traditionally herd reindeer.

clue.text: Not so loth to fade away and back out?

indicators.note: out puts the word for back on the outside, around the dying away

parts.note: rear means back
to die is to fade away

explanation.surface: Someone less reluctant to fade out and pull back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back out' looks like withdrawing, but it means REAR placed outside DIE: REA-DIE-R.
explanation.definitionFit: Being more willing or prepared is the opposite of being reluctant.

clue.text: Liquor that isn't drunk

parts.note: the dregs of drink left at the bottom of a glass, unconsumed rather than sober

explanation.surface: Alcohol that is not intoxicated.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the small amount of liquor left at the bottom of a glass after drinking.

clue.text: Badly rattled Aintree apprentice

indicators.note: badly rattled means shaken up, so the letters of the racecourse name are mixed

explanation.surface: A shaken novice at Aintree racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: Aintree is the Liverpool racecourse that hosts the Grand National.
explanation.definitionFit: A learner being taught a trade or job is an apprentice.

clue.text: Person responsible for the play reviews in the paper

definitions.text: Person responsible for the play reviews in the paper

parts.words: Person responsible for the play reviews in the paper
parts.note: play means games and matches, not theatre: the journalist in charge of a newspaper's coverage of games

explanation.surface: A newspaper's drama critic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' suggests theatre, but it means sporting play.
explanation.definitionFit: This journalist heads a newspaper's section covering games and athletics.
